Chicken (broiler) farms are the largest slice of BC’s poultry market. These are the questions that matter.
How does chicken quota work in BC?
Meat-chicken production is regulated by the

. Quota can transfer with registered premises or, in some cases, separately from the land — but both require an application and Board approval, and the premises must meet certification and approval requirements.

Quota does not simply run with the land. Any transfer must be applied for by both parties and approved by the applicable marketing board, and it isn’t included in a sale unless expressly stated in the Contract of Purchase and Sale.
Is the barn a factor in whether quota can transfer?
Very much so. The Board generally allots transferred quota only where it’s satisfied there’s a
. A farm’s barn size, condition, and approval status can decide whether a transfer proceeds at all — so they’re not just price factors, they’re deal factors.
What should I look for in a BC chicken farm?

Modern, well-ventilated barns sized to the quota; strong biosecurity; reliable water and power; efficient feed and manure systems; environmental compliance for runoff; and room to expand. The best operations are genuinely turn-key — a buyer can run cycles from day one.
